facts.statement: The only known species is Prodiplocynodon langi, which is represented by a single skull missing its lower jaw.
facts.quote: The only species of Prodiplocynodon is the type species P. langi from the Lance Formation of Wyoming, known only from a single holotype skull lacking the lower jaw.

facts.statement: The holotype skull was collected in 1892 by the American Museum Expedition near the Cheyenne River in Niobrara County.
facts.quote: The skull was collected by the American Museum Expedition of 1892 from exposures near the Cheyenne River in Niobrara County.

facts.statement: Charles C. Mook described the genus in 1941.
facts.quote: It was described by Charles C. Mook of the American Museum of Natural History in 1941.

facts.statement: The skull is short and triangular, measuring approximately 50 cm in length.
facts.quote: The skull is short and triangular, being around 50 cm in length.

facts.statement: The eye sockets are large and subtriangular in shape.
facts.quote: The orbits, or eye sockets, are quite large and subtriangular.

facts.statement: Its teeth are short and somewhat sharp, showing little variation compared to modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: The teeth are short and somewhat sharp, and in comparison to modern crocodiles show little variation.

facts.statement: The external opening for the nostrils is very large.
facts.quote: The external nasal aperture, the opening for the nostrils, is very large.

facts.statement: A constriction between the premaxilla and maxilla served as a reception area for a large lower jaw tooth.
facts.quote: There is a constriction at the point of contact between the premaxilla and maxilla which would have been an area of reception for a large mandibular tooth.

facts.statement: It is one of the few known crocodyloids from the Cretaceous, living during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: It is one of the only crocodyloids known from the Cretaceous and existed during the Maastrichtian stage.

facts.statement: It lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is classified as an extinct genus of basal crocodyloid crocodylian.
facts.quote: Prodiplocynodon is an extinct genus of basal crocodyloid crocodylian.

facts.statement: Mook suggested it might be ancestral to both alligatorids and crocodylids due to possessing features of both families.
facts.quote: Mook suggested that Prodiplocynodon may be ancestral to alligatorids and crocodylids because it possessed features of both families.

facts.statement: A 1996 study considered it the sister taxon to Alligatorinae rather than Crocodylinae.
facts.quote: The 1996 analysis considered Prodiplocynodon to be the sister taxon to the Alligatorinae rather than the Crocodylinae

facts.statement: Recent studies place it outside Crocodyloidea, as more basal than the group Longirostres.
facts.quote: The below cladogram shows the results of the latest studies, which placed Prodiplocynodon outside of Crocodyloidea, as more basal than Longirostres (the combined group of crocodiles and gavialids).

rejected.statement: The name 'Prodiplocynodon' means 'before Diplocynodon', reflecting similarities Mook noted with the Eocene alligatoroid Diplocynodon.
rejected.quote: The generic name means 'before Diplocynodon' because Mook saw close similarities between the holotype skull and that of the alligatoroid Diplocynodon from the Eocene of Europe.
